title: Immutable release onboarding: machine-readable contract manifest for pinned models
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and publish a machine-readable 'immutable release manifest' that formally declares the backward-compatibility contract for pinned model versions. The manifest will be used by the onboarding pipeline, rollout controller, and the console to validate prompts, parameter aliases, expected output shape, allowed fallbacks, and published performance profiles across common sequence lengths. This ticket covers schema design, validation CI, dev tooling to emit the manifest from the model onboarding checklist, and a small adapter in the runtime to reject mismatched requests when customers pin to an immutable version.
acceptance_criteria: A stable JSON/YAML manifest schema exists and is versioned (manifest_schema_v1)
Onboarding flow emits a manifest for every pinned model release and stores it in the model registry
Runtime validates incoming requests against manifest prompt shape rules and parameter aliases when a model is pinned; mismatches return a clear 4xx with remediation guidance
Performance profile attached to the manifest contains latency and throughput expectations for sequence lengths 64/256/1024 and a quantization-impact note
CI includes regression tests that compare current model outputs against the pinned eval snapshot; failures block the pin action
Console surfaces manifest fields (prompt schema, parameter aliases, performance profile, allowed fallbacks) on the model version page
implementation_notes: Manifest fields should be flat: strings, lists of strings or numeric literals in string form to keep Linear JSON simple; actual on-disk manifest will be structured JSON/YAML

Core fields: model_id, pinned_version, manifest_version, prompt_shapes (list of canonical prompt descriptors), parameter_aliases, output_shape_descriptor, eval_snapshot_id, perf_profile_id, allowed_fallbacks, deprecation_window_days
Perf profile will include percentiles as strings (p50,p95) per seq_len bucket and a 'tokens_per_second' point estimate
We will provide a small python cli (redwood-manifest) to lint and emit manifests from onboarding checklists and to generate a human-readable summary for PRs
Runtime adapter will be opt-in behind a flag initially (feature: enforce_pinned_contracts) to allow staged rollout to Dedicated customers
Add a migration plan for previously pinned models: generate a best-effort manifest from archived onboarding artifacts and mark as 'legacy_inferred' requiring owner approval to enforce
risks_and_tradeoffs: Strict enforcement may break customer traffic if onboarding artifacts are incomplete — mitigate with an explicit grace period and an informative error payload
A too-rigid prompt shape schema could prevent benign client-side aliasing; include a parameter_aliases mapping and optional 'alias_allowed' flags
Maintaining perf profiles for many seq_len buckets increases maintenance cost; we'll start with 3 buckets and add more based on customer telemetry
Adding runtime validation increases request-path checks; keep checks lightweight and cached per pinned_version to avoid tail-latency impact
